→ D1 (concedes): Conceded: F2 (closest approach 0 m at 08:43:00) and F4 (stationary 8 min 0 s at 0 m from pickup until 08:51:00) defeat my client's assertion that the driver never showed up; I do not build any claim on the complaint's non-arrival wording. [F2 F4] [NS-1]
→ D2: Accepted on the record, and it is the driver's advantage: F7 records a platform_auto confirmation at 08:43:00, so under NS-1 the arrival must be written as an automatic determination, not a driver button press — which is exactly why the NS-2 account flag for a tap made outside the pickup radius is not in play. [F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D3: Not conceded as to the result: NS-1(iii) requires continuous waiting 'until cancellation' on a measure the record must supply, and F8 shows the platform's own wait timer began at 08:43:10 with a 5 min 0 s free period expiring 08:48:10 and the fee applied at 08:51:00 — the judge must apply the threshold the case record carries, and the fact that the charge actually levied is $5.00 (F5, F9), an amount matching no published cancellation fee, is left unexplained by this claim. [F4 F6 F7 F8 F5 F9] [NS-1 NS-0]
→ D4: F1 and F3 support the continuous wait, but F1 also fixes the sampling at about 3 min 0 s, so each of the 8 samples is a point reading, not continuous observation; nothing in the record covers the rider's side of the pickup point, so the record cannot exclude a mutual miss at a mall of that size. [F1 F3] [NS-1]
→ D5: The fact is accepted — F17 (driver 4 messages, 1 call; rider 0 and 0) and F16 (complete, timestamped record) show no rider response — but NS-1 does not make the rider's silence an element of the charge; silence goes to the fee-waiver discretion under NS-7, not to the driver's entitlement. [F17 F16] [NS-1 NS-7]
→ D6: The lobby messages are the driver's own statements (F11, F12) and F2/F4 place the car 0 m from the pickup point, which is consistent with them; F15 nonetheless shows the warning came only at 08:50, two minutes before cancellation, after 7 minutes of waiting, so the rider had little time to act on it. [F11 F12 F15 F2 F4] [NS-1]
→ D7: The three NS-1 conditions are not fully made out on this record: the charge levied is $5.00 (F9), not the $6.61 cancellation fee NS-0 addresses, and F8 shows the platform applied it off its own 08:43:10 timer with a 5 min free period rather than off the NS-1 default of waiting more than 3 minutes after the arrival confirmation; the shortfall in the levied fee therefore cannot be legitimised by NS-1. [F5 F9 F8 F7 F4] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2 NS-7]
→ D8 (concedes): Conceded: nothing in F11–F15, F17 amounts to a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation has no footing and I do not ask for one. [F11 F15 F17] [SAFE-1 SAFE-2]
